objective: Derive an exact separated-piece boundary criterion and a component-transposition leaf repair, with an honest consequence for hypothetical vertex-minimal root counterexamples.

atomic_claims.text: Two star-colored pieces meeting only at their degree-one boundary vertex glue exactly under the three stated alternating-arm conditions.
If the two old neighbors of u are separated in H-u, one palette transposition on a whole side repairs any saturated six-color leaf obstruction.
The eight cross-palette side transpositions yield a repair cost at most min(floor(N_X/2),floor(N_Y/2)).
In a hypothetical vertex-minimal root counterexample, every leaf neighbor lies on a cycle of length at least five and its other neighbors have degree three.

assumptions: G is finite, simple and subcubic; v is a leaf with neighbor u; H=G-v is globally star colored.
The repair lemma assumes that the two neighbors of u are in different components of H-u when d_H(u)=2.
The critical-graph consequence is conditional on vertex-minimal failure of the root.
risks: The separator hypothesis excludes the unresolved cyclic case.
One transposition can change many old edges; no universal constant edit bound is asserted.
Simultaneous recoloring need not admit a valid one-edge-at-a-time sequence.
The critical-graph consequence does not assert minimum degree two.
No mathematical execution or verification receipt is claimed.
